**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 8, §8.3. This tutorial uses independent wording, derivations and order data.

## The question we need to answer

The same delivery model can be fitted by minimising prediction error or by maximising a probability model for observations. Different assumptions may lead to the same numerical estimator.

## Formal relationship

$$
\hat{\theta}_{\rm MLE}=\arg\max_\theta p(\mathcal D\mid\theta),\quad\hat{\theta}_{\rm MAP}=\arg\max_\theta p(\mathcal D\mid\theta)p(\theta)
$$

The notation makes the assumptions and dependencies explicit. Check that the variables, sets and dimensions match the running example before drawing a conclusion.

## Derive the answer from the example

Suppose y1=12 and y2=14 are independent Gaussian observations with known variance. Maximising their likelihood over a common mean gives μ-hat=(12+14)/2=13. Adding a normal prior pulls the MAP estimate toward the prior mean.

## Interpretation and limitations

MLE and MAP select point estimates, whereas full Bayesian inference carries parameter uncertainty forward. Both require a meaningful likelihood, and a prior expresses additional assumptions.

## Explain it yourself

When does MAP coincide with MLE? Describe the role of a constant prior on the parameter domain.
